title.es: Multi-criteria journey planning on the passenger's device: design and validation for fifteen merged regional transit networks
title.en: Multi-criteria journey planning on the passenger's device: design and validation for fifteen merged regional transit networks
title.eu: Multi-criteria journey planning on the passenger's device: design and validation for fifteen merged regional transit networks

tldr.es: Un planificador de rutas de transporte público que calcula todo en el propio móvil, sin servidor, sobre quince redes de Euskadi y alrededores fusionadas (8.242 paradas). Funciona sin conexión, corrige los resultados con el tiempo real y responde en una mediana de 16 ms en un iPhone reciente y 65 ms en un Android de gama media de 2021.
tldr.en: A public transport journey planner that computes everything on the passenger's phone, with no server, over fifteen merged networks in and around the Basque Country (8,242 stops). It works offline, repairs answers with real-time data and answers in a median of 16 ms on a recent iPhone and 65 ms on a 2021 mid-range Android phone.
tldr.eu: Garraio publikoko ibilbide-planifikatzaile bat, dena bidaiariaren mugikorrean kalkulatzen duena, zerbitzaririk gabe, Euskal Herriko eta inguruko hamabost sare bateratuen gainean (8.242 geraleku). Konexiorik gabe dabil, emaitzak denbora errealarekin zuzentzen ditu eta 16 ms-ko medianan erantzuten du iPhone berri batean eta 65 ms-koan 2021eko erdi-mailako Android batean.

scholar.eyebrow: Preprint v1.0 · Journey Planning · Open Access (CC BY 4.0)
scholar.metaDescription: A multi-criteria journey planner that runs entirely on the passenger's device, in the browser, over fifteen merged transit networks in the Basque Country: validated against Connection Scan and OpenTripPlanner, 16 ms median plan query on a recent iPhone.
scholar.ogDescription: On-device multi-criteria journey planning over 15 merged transit networks (8,242 stops): offline, real-time repair, 16 ms median query on iPhone, 65 ms on a 2021 Android.
scholar.archiveSummary: Design and validation of a multi-criteria range RAPTOR planner that runs entirely in the browser on the passenger's phone, over fifteen merged transit networks in and around the Basque Country (8,242 stops, 54,896 trips). Four labels per bag find 88% of the exact restricted Pareto set, lower bounds make plan queries 2.6 times faster, earliest arrivals agree with Connection Scan, and with the production walking table it returns 96% of OpenTripPlanner's journeys within 60 s. Median plan query: 16 ms on a recent iPhone, 65 ms on a 2021 mid-range Android phone.
scholar.abstract: Journey planners for public transport usually compute routes on a server. This paper describes and evaluates one that computes them entirely on the passenger’s device, in the browser, over fifteen merged transit networks in and around the Basque Country (8,242 stops, 54,896 trips). Offline it answers from the last timetables downloaded; online it repairs each answer with the real-time state of the trips shown. Its search is a multi-criteria range variant of round-based public transit routing on arrival and walking time, with bags of four labels that never discard the earliest arrival and lower bounds on the remaining time and rides computed once per target; a selection layer turns the result into five labelled options. On the production data, four labels find 88% of the exact restricted Pareto set without changing the first option of 2,000 plan queries, and the bounds make plan queries 2.6 times faster. Earliest arrivals agree with an independent Connection Scan search and with an exhaustive enumeration of small networks. Against OpenTripPlanner on identical data and without pruning of walking options, each planner returns almost every journey of the other that its own walking rules allow, to within 60 s (ours) and 120 s (OpenTripPlanner); with the production walking table, ours returns 96% of those of OpenTripPlanner within 60 s. Delaying or cancelling a third of the trips adds half to the query time. In single runs, the median plan query took 16 ms on a recent iPhone and 65 ms on a 2021 mid-range Android phone.

title.es: Accuracy of open-data versus operator real-time bus arrival predictions: a paired evaluation of the Bide+ method in Biscay, Spain
title.en: Accuracy of open-data versus operator real-time bus arrival predictions: a paired evaluation of the Bide+ method in Biscay, Spain
title.eu: Accuracy of open-data versus operator real-time bus arrival predictions: a paired evaluation of the Bide+ method in Biscay, Spain

tldr.es: Comparamos más de medio millón de llegadas reales de Bizkaibus (555.744 mediciones por GPS): nuestro sistema queda a ±2 min del paso real en el 64 % de los casos, frente al 39 % de la app oficial y el 16 % del horario; a partir de tres minutos, acierta más en 57 de las 59 paradas.
tldr.en: We compared over half a million real Bizkaibus arrivals (555,744 GPS measurements): our open-data method is within ±2 min of the actual passage in 64% of cases, versus 39% for the official app and 16% for the timetable; from three minutes out, it is ahead at 57 of 59 stops.
tldr.eu: Bizkaibus-eko milioi erdi baino gehiago iritsiera erreal alderatu ditugu (555.744 GPS neurketa): gure metodoa benetako igarotzetik ±2 minutura dago kasuen %64an, app ofizialaren %39aren eta ordutegiaren %16aren aurrean; hiru minututik aurrera, 59tik 57 geralekutan hobea da.

scholar.eyebrow: Preprint v1.0 · Empirical Paired Evaluation · Open Access (CC BY 4.0)
scholar.metaDescription: Paired evaluation of 555,744 real-time bus arrival predictions in Biscay, Spain: within ±2 minutes of the actual passage in 16% of cases for the timetable, 39% for the operator's real time and 64% for the open-data Bide+ method.
scholar.ogDescription: 555,744 paired predictions on Bizkaibus: within ±2 min in 16% (timetable), 39% (official real time) and 64% (Bide+, open data only).
scholar.archiveSummary: Paired empirical benchmark of 555,744 real-time arrival predictions against GPS ground truth across 59 stops in Biscay (Bizkaibus). Within ±2 minutes of the actual passage: 16% for the timetable, 39% for the official real time and 64% for the open-data Bide+ method; from three minutes out, Bide+ is more often within ±2 minutes at 57 of 59 stops.
scholar.abstract: This paper compares an operator’s real-time bus predictions with an independent predictor for the same buses at the same moments, for Bizkaibus, the interurban network of Biscay (Spain), which publishes vehicle positions and timetable as open data and shows its own waiting times in an app. For one week in November 2026, the official waiting times of 60 stops were recorded every minute with the position feed. Each official announcement was matched to the bus it referred to, confirmed by the distance the service reports, and compared with the published timetable and with the Bide+ method, which predicts arrivals from the open data alone and was frozen before the week. All three were checked against the actual passage, reconstructed from the feed and from GPS positions. Across 555,744 paired predictions on six days, the timetable was within two minutes of the actual passage in 16% of cases, the official real time in 39% and Bide+ in 64%. Below three minutes the two real-time sources were equally often within two minutes, although the official one had the smaller mean error below six minutes; from three minutes on, Bide+ was more often within two minutes, by 29 to 35 percentage points at 10–20 minutes (95% interval by stop), at 57 of 59 stops and at every hour. An ablation attributes its advantage to learned segment travel times. The results apply to the 54% of first-bus announcements whose bus was tracked and confirmed, and to one week; data and code are open.

title.es: Predicting bus arrivals when the feed reports positions but not delays: a reproducible three-layer method with an open reference implementation
title.en: Predicting bus arrivals when the feed reports positions but not delays: a reproducible three-layer method with an open reference implementation
title.eu: Predicting bus arrivals when the feed reports positions but not delays: a reproducible three-layer method with an open reference implementation

tldr.es: Cómo calcular cuándo llega un autobús usando solo su posición GPS cuando los datos públicos no indican el retraso. En 9,1 millones de predicciones, la llegada cae a ±2 min en el 92–96 % de los casos cuando el bus está a menos de tres minutos (67 % a 10–20 min, frente al 23–25 % del horario), con código abierto en Python.
tldr.en: How to predict bus arrival times using only live GPS positions when public feeds omit delays. In 9.1 million predictions, the arrival shown is within ±2 min in 92–96% of cases when the bus is under three minutes away (67% at 10–20 min, vs 23–25% for the timetable), with open Python code.
tldr.eu: Autobus bat noiz iritsiko den nola kalkulatu GPS posizioa soilik erabiliz datu publikoek atzerapenik ematen ez dutenean. 9,1 milioi aurreikuspenetan, iritsiera ±2 minututan dago kasuen %92–96an autobusa hiru minutu baino gutxiagora dagoenean (%67 10–20 minututan, ordutegiaren %23–25aren aurrean), Python kode irekiarekin.

scholar.eyebrow: Preprint v1.1 · Method Specification · Open Access (CC BY 4.0 & MIT)
scholar.metaDescription: Three-layer bus arrival prediction method with explicit abstention for feeds that report GPS positions but not delays. In 9.1 million predictions over 23 days, the arrival shown is within ±2 min in 92–96% of cases when the bus is under three minutes away and in 67% at 10–20 minutes, against 23–25% for the published timetable.
scholar.ogDescription: Three-layer ETA method for feeds without delays. 9.1M predictions: within ±2 min in 92–96% of cases under three minutes out and 67% at 10–20 minutes, vs 23–25% for the published timetable.
scholar.archiveSummary: Formal specification and open Python reference implementation of a three-layer arrival prediction method with explicit abstention and shrunk learned travel-time medians for SIRI-VM/GTFS feeds that omit schedule deviations. In 9.1 million predictions, within ±2 minutes in 92–96% of cases when the bus is under three minutes away and 67% at 10–20 minutes, against 23–25% for the published timetable.
scholar.abstract: Many public transport networks publish real-time vehicle positions but not delays, and many timetables give intermediate stop times interpolated at constant speed rather than observed. Bizkaibus, the interurban bus network of Biscay (Spain), has both properties: after the first hour of a trip, 85% of buses pass a stop more than two minutes before the published time. This paper specifies the arrival prediction method of the Bizkaibus+ app in enough detail to reimplement it in any language. The method uses timetable differences instead of absolute times; learns the actual travel time between consecutive stops by time band, as a median shrunk towards the all-day median of the segment; and predicts from three layers with explicit abstention rules: the GPS position projected onto the route, the last stop registered by the feed, and the timetable corrected trip by trip. It recalibrates itself daily, adopting only changes that reduce the error on held-out data. In 9.1 million predictions over 23 days, checked against the actual passage, the arrival shown is within ±2 minutes in 92–96% of cases when the bus is less than three minutes away and in 67% at ten to twenty minutes, against 23–25% for the published timetable. Without any live data, the corrected timetable alone doubles the accuracy of the published one. A reference implementation in Python, test vectors with 407 checks produced by the production engine, a public evaluator that reproduces the production histograms, and the learned tables and evaluation data are openly available.

title.es: Predicción de llegadas de autobuses con posiciones en tiempo real y horarios interpolados
title.en: Bus arrival prediction from real-time positions and interpolated timetables
title.eu: Autobusen iritsiera-aurreikuspena denbora errealeko posizioekin eta interpolatutako ordutegiekin

tldr.es: Libro técnico completo de 200 páginas donde se explica toda la ingeniería y matemáticas del motor predictivo (incluyendo filtrado de Kalman, red neuronal que reduce el error medio un 6–7 % y 407 pruebas verificables).
tldr.en: Complete 200-page technical monograph documenting the full engineering and mathematics behind the prediction engine (including Kalman filtering, a neural network cutting mean error by 6–7%, and 407 verified tests).
tldr.eu: 200 orrialdeko memoria tekniko osoa, iragarpen-motorraren ingeniaritza eta matematika guztiak azaltzen dituena (Kalman iragazkia, batez besteko errorea %6–7 murrizten duen sare neuronala eta 407 proba egiaztagarri).

scholar.eyebrow: Memoria Técnica v2.1 · 200 Páginas · Acceso Abierto (CC BY 4.0 & MIT)
scholar.metaDescription: Memoria técnica de 200 páginas sobre el método de predicción de llegadas de Bizkaibus+/Bide+: en 2,21 millones de predicciones, la llegada cae dentro de ±2 min en el 96 % a menos de tres minutos y en el 67 % entre diez y veinte minutos, frente al 24–25 % del horario publicado.
scholar.ogDescription: Memoria técnica de 200 páginas: método en tres capas con abstención, filtro de Kalman y red neuronal (−6–7 % de error medio), 407 vectores de prueba e implementación de referencia.
scholar.archiveSummary: Memoria técnica exhaustiva de 200 páginas: formulación matemática completa del motor de predicción ETA, filtro de Kalman sobre ritmo de marcha, red neuronal que reduce el error medio de las sumas de tramos un 6–7 %, 407 vectores de prueba y código de referencia abierto en Python.
scholar.abstract: Bizkaibus, la red de autobuses interurbanos de Bizkaia, publica la posición GPS de cada vehículo y su próxima parada, pero no su retraso. Las horas intermedias de su horario oficial están interpoladas a velocidad constante: de 169 308 pasos reales por parada, el 85 % de los que ocurren pasada la primera hora de viaje llega más de dos minutos antes de la hora publicada. Esta memoria describe, para que pueda replicarse, el método con que la aplicación Bizkaibus+ predice las llegadas. El método trabaja con diferencias de horario en lugar de horas absolutas, aprende el tiempo real de cada tramo por franja horaria con medianas contraídas y organiza la predicción en tres capas con reglas de abstención: la posición proyectada sobre el recorrido, la última parada registrada y el horario corregido viaje a viaje. Se recalibra cada día y solo adopta cambios que reducen el error. En 2,21 millones de predicciones a menos de veinte minutos, de 17 días, contrastadas con el paso real, la llegada mostrada cae dentro de ±2 minutos en el 96 % cuando el autobús está a menos de tres minutos y en el 67 % entre diez y veinte minutos, frente al 24 % y el 25 % del horario publicado. Evaluados por días, un filtro de Kalman sobre el ritmo del propio autobús y una red neuronal reducen el error medio de las sumas de tramos un 4 % y entre un 6 y un 7 %, respectivamente. Se incluyen vectores de prueba y una implementación de referencia que los reproduce.
